name: warmstart_01 warmstart=2 dual values
comment: Drivers passing dual start values to the solver

name: knap_40_pstart partial MIP start native
comment: HiGHS completes the partial start itself (mip:start=1); with lim:nodes=0 the completed start (766) stays the incumbent
output: MIP start solution is feasible, objective value is 766

name: knap_40_pstart partial MIP start legacy
comment: Driver-side completion (mip:start=2): fix the given values, solve, unfix, pass the complete start; no node limit because the completion sub-solve inherits it
output: MIP start solution is feasible, objective value is 766

name: knap_40_pstart partial MIP start maxstartnodes=0
comment: The start cannot be completed within 0 nodes and is dropped; with lim:nodes=0 no incumbent results

name: nlp_warmstart_01
comment: The 2nd solve allows no major iterations: 'solved' only if the warm start is accepted

name: nlp_warmstart_01 cold start
comment: Negative control: without the incoming basis and point the 2nd solve hits the limit

name: ws_hint_01 alg:start=0 fixed to hints CP-SAT
comment: Negative control: no hints, so nothing is fixed

name: warmstart_ind_01 primal-dual start with indicators
comment: Primal and dual initial values, no statuses: drivers that keep indicators as solver rows must still pass one dual per solver row

name: pstart_nl_01 primal start only
comment: Primal initial values without dual values reach the driver; solvers keeping the model continuous

name: pstart_nl_01 alg:startpartial=0
comment: Negative control: the old behavior needs dual values too. The option goes to the tested driver only: an MP subsolver of MP2NL would also read mp_options

name: pstart_nl_01 NL barrier Gurobi
comment: Gurobi's NL barrier loads the primal start (PStart). The local minimum reached depends on the version (13.0.3: -2.2512669, 14.0.0: -1.9194447), but differs from the cold start

name: pstart_nl_01 NL barrier alg:start=0 Gurobi
comment: Negative control: Gurobi's default start leads to this local minimum (13.0.3 and 14.0.0)

name: pstart_nl_02 no constraints NL barrier Gurobi
comment: Without constraints AMPL cannot send dual values; the primal start leads to this local minimum (13.0.3 and 14.0.0)

name: pstart_nl_02 no constraints alg:startpartial=0 Gurobi
comment: Negative control: the old behavior ignores the primal start without dual values. Gurobi's default start depends on the version and on how the driver passes the model (-2.0839839 or -1.5986054 seen), so check that the result differs from the warm-start one

name: pstart_lp_01 primal start only
comment: Primal initial values without dual values are passed to the solver

name: pstart_lp_01 primal start only COPT
comment: COPT takes an LP start only with primal and dual values: a warning
output: Incoming primal start values not used

name: pstart_lp_01 alg:startpartial=0
comment: Negative control: the old behavior needs dual values too

name: pstart_lp_01 primal simplex Gurobi
comment: Gurobi's primal simplex uses the primal start alone (PStart, no DStart)

name: dstart_lp_01 dual start only
comment: Dual initial values without primal values are passed to the solver

name: dstart_lp_01 dual start only not passed
comment: Drivers not passing dual values alone: a warning
output: Incoming dual start values not used

name: dstart_lp_01 alg:startpartial=0
comment: Negative control: the old behavior needs primal values too

name: dstart_lp_01 dual simplex Gurobi
comment: Gurobi's dual simplex uses the dual start alone (DStart, no PStart)

name: mipstart_fixed_01 presolve=0
comment: All integer variables fixed: no unfixed integer variables, primal start only; CP-SAT must not get duplicate hints

name: mipstart_fixed_01 presolve=0 no warning
comment: The primal values reach the solver (as an LP or a MIP start): no warning. Not COPT: MP passes the fixed integer variables as continuous, COPT solves an LP and takes an LP start only with dual values (see pstart_lp_01 primal start only COPT)

name: pstart_sos_01 primal start, native SOS
comment: No integer variables, but a MIP for solvers with native SOS: the primal values go to the MIP start, no warning

name: resolve_lp_01 re-solve without warnings
comment: The second solve gets primal and dual values: no warning, also from drivers that pass primal values only
